newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel girls militant about watching TV soap.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel girls militant about watching TV soap.

text.p: Two teenage girls in a Marxist rebel group holding scores of VIP hostages in Peru were just as concerned about missing their favourite soap opera as guarding their captives, a former hostage said on Sunday.
"They'd shout, 'Leave it there!' if one of us tried to change the channel," university profesor Carlos Aquino Rodriguez told Reuters.
Any thoughts of challenging the girls' viewing tastes were dispelled by the sight of the AKM rifles lying across their laps, he added.

The girls, both from Peru's jungle region and aged around 16 or 17, were particularly fond of "Maria From the Barrio," a Mexican soap about a poor but beautiful girl trying to overcome her impoverished background.
"They knew all the characters. They'd say, 'He's the bad one' or 'She's in love with him.' They really enjoyed it," Aquino said.

One of the teenagers, assigned to guard Aquino and 27 others, said she had developed a taste for television while holed up in a Lima hideout in the weeks leading up to the rebels' spectacular assult on a lavish reception at the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17.

"They'd rarely seen television before, as they are from the jungle," said Aquino, who was released by the guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) on Dec. 22 along with 224 other hostages.
The young rebels also enjoyed televison commercials, frequently singing along to the music and laughing, he said.
The two girls were part of a 20-strong band of mainly young MRTA rebels who still held 83 hostages at the residence on Sunday.
